words.prose: {{ar:فُجِّرَتْ}} ({{tr:fujjirat}}) lands the ayah on forced breach. Its Form II passive keeps causative pressure while suppressing the visible causer, so {{ar:ٱلْبِحَارُ}} ({{tr:al-biḥāru}}) carries the event on the surface as one affected patient. Under {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), the perfect form makes the rupture vivid and complete while the larger condition still waits for 82:5. The root image is not ordinary overflow: pressure meets a boundary, the boundary gives way, and release follows. Wider root relatives such as dawn-splitting and moral breach sharpen the shared boundary logic, while local grammar keeps the seas physical rather than moral agents. Variant evidence shows the pressure points: {{ar:فُجِرَتْ}} ({{tr:fujirat}}) would lighten the doubled force, and {{ar:فَجَرَتْ}} ({{tr:fajarat}}) would make the seas burst as subject, while the main reading stacks intensity with hidden causation. Its sound gathers pressure at the doubled center, releases through the rolling middle, and closes sharply at the final stop. That rare passive sea-breach profile makes this root realization marked rather than default. At the boundary with 82:2, the movement shifts from upper arrangement scattering outward to lower containment being forced open. The parallels also matter: provisionary bursting in {{ar:اِنْفَجَرَتْ}} ({{tr:infajarat}}) at 2:60 is reversed into cosmic unmaking here, and {{ar:فَفَجَّرْنَا}} ({{tr:fa-fajjarnā}}) at 54:12 names the opener where 82:3 withholds one. The same root returns in {{ar:ٱلْفُجَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-fujjār}}) at 82:14, linking cosmic containment failure to human boundary-breaking without collapsing the two senses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Broad waters burst their channels.** `البحار` anchors **ب ح ر B001** (“wide abundant water”), while `فجرت` anchors **ف ج ر B001** (“wide splitting and outflow”). The two branch images supply both stored expanse and forcible outlet; I infer that breached boundaries convert containment into flow. The ayah reads as hydraulic release, not a generic disturbance of seas.

2. **Cleft and outflow activate each other.** **ب ح ر B003** (“wide cleft”) is dormant in the sea noun but structurally paired with **ف ج ر B001**. The packet supplies adjacent cleft and splitting images; I infer that the sea becomes both what is opened and the opening through which contents pass. This yields a spatial reading in which established basins cease to separate domains.

3. **Physical breach anticipates moral breach.** The same root returns in `الفجار` at 82:14, where **ف ج ر B004** means departure from right and breach of restraint. The packet supplies the root recurrence and the physical/moral branches; I infer a shared mechanism of crossing a restraining boundary. The sea’s bursting becomes a material analogue for agents later defined by breached restraint, without collapsing the two readings into one.

4. **The hidden becomes exposed.** **ب ح ر B005** (“open exposure”) is activated by the immediately following graves being upturned in 82:4. The packet supplies exposure and extraction images; I infer that bursting removes the surfaces that kept contents out of view. The ayah can therefore signal disclosure as well as flooding.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Verse 82:14 is the decisive retrospective surprise: `الفجار` converts the current physical breach into a model of moral boundary-breaking. The record and reckoning in 82:10–15 then show why exposure matters.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Contained waters are opened into outflow.** `ب ح ر B001` supplies broad, abundant water, and `ف ج ر B001` supplies a wide split, bursting water, and opened channels. The preceding sky and stars lose enclosure and arrangement; the following graves lose the earth that covers them. The packet gives this parallel sequence, while I infer that each passive marks the failure of a different containing system. The seas therefore read as reservoirs whose boundaries are opened into channels, not simply as water made turbulent.

2. **The sea becomes exposed space.** `ب ح ر B005` gives open exposure with no screen, while `ف ج ر B001` provides the physical breach. Proximity to 82:4-5, where hidden grave contents become known to a self, turns exposure into the functional role of the burst. I infer that opening the seas removes their capacity to screen depth, just as overturning graves removes the earth's capacity to screen burial. The fixed ayah consequently joins an epistemic mechanism: what was deep and covering becomes openly encounterable.

3. **A deep vessel in the sequence of forced emergence.** `ب ح ر B007` includes depth of the womb, and `ف ج ر B001` gives a wide opening and outflow. The nearby womb activations in `ر ح م B003` and `ن ث ر B006`, followed by creation and bodily composition in 82:7-8, supply a material cluster of containment, formation, and release. I supply the exploratory analogy that sea-depth functions as a vast gestational vessel. The bursting seas can then be read as another scale of forced emergence, linking cosmic disassembly to the later reappearance of embodied selves.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 82:14's *fujjar* later activated the same root's `ف ج ر B004` branch of moral breach. That recurrence made the sea's `ف ج ر B001` physical outflow a material model for restraint broken in conduct; 82:15-16 then supplied the corrective limit, an outcome from which the boundary-breakers cannot be absent.

findings.text: Denizlerin yarılması, birikmiş geniş suların sınırları açılarak kanallara ve zorlayıcı akışa dönüşmesidir.
Yarılma, denizlerin derinlikleri örten yüzey olma işlevini kaldırarak saklı olanı açıkta bırakır.
Havzalar açıldığında deniz hem yarılan şey hem de içinden geçilen yarık haline gelir; böylece alanları ayırma işlevi sona erer.
Denizin sınırını aşıp taşması, daha sonra kötüler diye anılanların ahlaki sınır aşımının maddi örneğine dönüşür.
Deniz derinliğinin geniş bir rahim gibi açılması, kozmik çözülmeyi bedenlerin yeniden ortaya çıkışına bağlayan zorlanmış bir doğum imgesi olarak düşünülebilir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A closed, ordered, or concealed arrangement is opened, scattered, overturned, or made visible.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Fissure and Forceful Opening

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Each motif supplies a distinct material instance of the same operation: an intact boundary becomes a passage. The bodily cleft and cut ear preserve the concrete morphology of the cosmic and hydrological rupture.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: ب ح ر at 82:3; ع ل م at 82:5/12; ر ب ب at 82:6.

facets.statement: Kişi doğruluk ve inanç sınırlarını çiğneyerek doğru yoldan sapar.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_focus_trace_hermetic.note: Hermetic Focus Trace not requested for this bundle. Rebuild with --include-focus-trace, or --require-focus-trace when reader JSON must be present.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
